nuggets.title: Flash Sale Double-Books the Same Seat

scenario.symptoms: Concert on-sale generates 200 support tickets for duplicate seat assignments. Two confirmation emails reference seat A-12 for different orders.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Seat hold uses read-modify-write in application code without transactional locking or unique constraint on (event_id, seat_id) for confirmed state.

incident.headline: Non-atomic seat reservation allows two confirmations for one physical seat

agenda.goal: Reserve seats with atomic conditional updates or serializable transactions and unique sold constraints.
agenda.opener: Two customers got the same seat during on-sale. How do you prevent double booking under concurrent load?

evidence.strong: UPDATE ... WHERE status=available with row count check, unique partial index on sold seats, serializable isolation or per-event locking shard, idempotent order id.
evidence.adequate: Application mutex in one API instance only.
evidence.weak: Check availability then insert in two steps without lock.

misconceptions.pattern: Relies on cache of available seats without DB authority.
misconceptions.challenge: Who wins if two servers read 'available' simultaneously?

probes: Where is the source of truth for seat state?
How do you test race conditions?
agenda.referenceFix: Atomic update seat row, unique constraint on confirmed seats, shard lock per hot event.

nuggets.title: Abandoned Holds Lock Inventory for Hours

scenario.symptoms: Show appears sold out while UI shows 400 seats in 'held' state. Revenue lost because holds from abandoned carts never expire.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Hold TTL job crashed three days ago; holds persist until manual cleanup. No heartbeat extends only active checkout sessions.

incident.headline: Failed hold expiration leaves inventory locked in abandoned checkout states

agenda.goal: Time-bound holds with reliable TTL sweeper, session heartbeat, and lazy expiry on read.
agenda.opener: The show looked sold out but hundreds of seats were stuck in holds from abandoned carts. How do temporary holds work?

evidence.strong: Hold expires_at indexed, redundant sweeper + lazy check on purchase, heartbeat extends active checkout only, metrics on hold age, max hold duration.
evidence.weak: Holds until payment completes with no timeout.

misconceptions.pattern: Treats hold as soft reservation with no hard expiry.
misconceptions.challenge: What if user closes laptop mid-checkout?

hints: Lazy expiry on next sale attempt.
agenda.referenceFix: TTL with dual expiry paths, alert on sweeper lag, cap holds per session.

nuggets.title: Stale Read Replica Shows Seats as Available

scenario.symptoms: Seat map API shows green available seats that fail at payment with 'already sold'. Replica lag averages 8 seconds during on-sale.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Interactive seat map reads from async replica; writes go to primary. Users browse on stale view then hit primary on commit.

incident.headline: Serving seat availability from lagging replicas misleads users during high write load

agenda.goal: Scale reads without stale inventory using primary for hot paths, caching with invalidation, or CRDT-style version checks.
agenda.opener: Users see seats available on the map but checkout says sold. How do you scale seat map reads during on-sale?

evidence.strong: Primary or strongly consistent read for availability, cache with pub/sub invalidation on sell, version token on map vs purchase, separate read scale for static venue layout only.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes read replicas are always fresh enough.
misconceptions.challenge: What lag is acceptable when seats sell per second?

probes: Which reads can be eventually consistent?
How do you invalidate seat map cache on sell?
hints: Hot inventory path needs authoritative reads.
agenda.referenceFix: Consistent availability reads on primary or cache with instant invalidation; replicas for historical analytics only.

nuggets.title: Payment Captured but Booking Record Missing

scenario.symptoms: Payment provider shows 1,200 successful captures without matching confirmed orders in booking DB after DB failover during on-sale.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Checkout commits payment then writes order in separate step without outbox or reconciliation job; crash between steps loses linkage.

incident.headline: Non-atomic payment and booking flow leaves captured charges without confirmed tickets

agenda.goal: Make booking idempotent with transactional outbox, saga, and payment reconciliation jobs.
agenda.opener: Customers were charged but have no tickets after the outage. How do payment and seat confirmation stay consistent?

evidence.strong: Idempotent checkout id, reserve seat then pay then confirm in saga with compensating refund, outbox for async confirm, nightly payment-order reconciliation.
evidence.weak: Charge first hope DB write succeeds.

misconceptions.pattern: Captures payment before seat is durably reserved.
misconceptions.challenge: If DB fails after charge, what does customer have?

probes: What is the idempotency key for checkout?
How do you detect orphan captures?
hints: Outbox ties payment webhook to order.
agenda.referenceFix: Saga: hold seat, authorize, confirm order, capture; reconciliation refunds orphan charges.
